subject: Private deployment constraints & audit access — NetZero Health (NZ-2384)
messages:
From: Marta Alvarez <marta@netzerohealth.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@netzerohealth.com, security@netzerohealth.com
Date: Fri, 3 Jul 2026 09:12:00 +0200
Subject: Private on‑prem + audit scope for NZ‑2384

Hi David,

Thanks again for the call this morning. As we discussed, NetZero Health is proceeding with a private on‑prem deployment for our EU clinical workloads (PHI/PII). Before legal proceeds we need written confirmation on the following items to move the SOW forward: 

- Data residency: all production data must remain in our EU cluster(s).
- Egress: no outbound internet from the workload hosts (except to our approved monitoring endpoints).
- Audit rights: monthly access for our security auditors (onsite or remote) plus a snapshot of audit logs for a rolling 12 months.
- HSM/KMS: we need integration with our HSM for key material used for token encryption.
- Patching: cannot have automatic external package updates without our change control approval.

I've attached NetZero's security requirements and a draft SOW for reference (NZH_Security_Requirements_2026.pdf, SOW_NZH_v0.4.docx). We also want to request consideration for a 20% discount as part of a 36‑month committed contract to offset the custom engineering and compliance work.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept these constraints and whether any of the items will require executive signoff?

Best,
Marta
Marta Alvarez
Head of IT Security, NetZero Health
-- attachment: NZH_Security_Requirements_2026.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)
-- attachment: SOW_NZH_v0.4.docx (DOCX, 120KB)

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: Marta Alvarez <marta@netzerohealth.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Jul 2026 11:05:00 +02:00
Subject: Fwd: Private on‑prem + audit scope for NZ‑2384

Folks — forwarding NetZero's asks. Summary below and an explicit ask for exec approval:

NetZero asks that we:
1) Enforce EU‑only residency for production data.
2) Block general outbound internet; allow a limited set of monitoring/metrics endpoints.
3) Provide monthly auditor access (onsite/remote) + 12‑month audit log snapshots.
4) Integrate with customer HSM for token/secret material.
5) Disable automatic external package updates unless approved by their change board.
6) Customer asks for 20% discount on a 36‑month commit to fund engineering work.

Initial notes: residency + egress constraints are doable via Private deployment options. HSM integration is feasible but likely a multi‑week engineering effort. Monthly auditor access is sensitive — legal will want to limit scope and require NDA + SOC2 evidence. The 20% discount materially impacts margin; Sales Ops needs exec intake.

Can you weigh in on (a) legal redlines needed, (b) what discount we can offer without Deal Desk escalation, and (c) whether we can commit to the requested audit cadence?

I'll coordinate a short call with the NetZero security team if that helps.

Thanks,
David
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 3 Jul 2026 13:30:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private on‑prem + audit scope for NZ‑2384

David / Markus — reviewed the security requirements. Flags and suggested contract language below.

Main legal flags: 
- Auditor access: "monthly" onsite access is very broad. Propose: quarterly audit windows with a defined 4‑hour remote session or a single onsite visit per quarter (subject to scheduling). Require written scope and redaction rights for any PII in auditor reports.
- Egress/no internet: we can support a constrained egress policy but must retain emergency outbound for critical patches and telemetry to Redwood ops endpoints — propose an approved endpoints list and change‑control process.
- HSM integration: acceptable but will be an approved integration project with additional SOW and a one‑time integration fee; we need to limit Redwood liability where keys are customer‑controlled.
- Data residency: we can commit contractually to EU region for production storage and backups.

Pricing/discounts: 20% on list price for a 36‑month committed term is out of standard approval for Sales Ops. Recommend asking for an executive approval; suggest offering 12–15% discount plus a one‑time implementation fee to cover engineering and compliance work.

Proposed redlines to include in SOW:
1) Defined "Audit Window" schedule and scope.
2) List of approved egress endpoints; change‑control ticket pathway.
3) HSM integration SOW & implementation fee; limited liability clause for key material.
4) 12‑15% committed term discount + implementation fee (line item).

If Exec approves 15% and the SOW fee, Legal can prepare redlines tomorrow. Otherwise we escalate to Laura for final approval.

— Lauren
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 3 Jul 2026 15:00:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private on‑prem + audit scope for NZ‑2384

Adding the commercial picture:
- Baseline ARR for NZ‑2384 (36 mo) at list is EUR 2,400,000.
- 20% discount would reduce ARR to EUR 1,920,000 — gross margin impact is significant given the one‑time engineering and ongoing operational overhead.
- Implementation/engineering estimate: 7–9 weeks of effort (security, infra, QA) — we should charge a fixed implementation fee (~EUR 180k) or time & materials with cap.
- If Exec will sign off only on 15% discount + EUR 150k implementation fee we get to acceptable economics.

I recommend we present NetZero with: 15% committed term discount, EUR 150k one‑time SOW fee, and defined audit windows (quarterly) with an option to buy additional audit sessions. This meets most security asks while protecting margin.

Markus
Head of Sales Operations

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>, lauren_bishop@redwood.com, markus_klein@markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 3 Jul 2026 17:22:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Private on‑prem + audit scope for NZ‑2384

David / Lauren / Markus — thank you for the summary. I will approve the commercial package with the following executive conditions: 

1) Discount: approve up to 15% committed term discount for a 36‑month contract.
2) Implementation fee: require a non‑negotiable one‑time SOW fee of EUR 150,000 to cover HSM integration and deployment customizations.
3) Audit access: change "monthly auditor access" to defined quarterly audit windows (customer may purchase additional audit sessions at a published rate). Onsite auditors allowed once per year; otherwise remote sessions. Redaction rights apply and Redwood retains right to redact PII from produced materials.
4) Egress & patching: allow restricted egress list. Patching will be coordinated under a change control board; Redwood reserves the right to push critical security patches to maintain platform integrity (we will notify customer in advance where possible).

Legal to issue redlines for the SOW and T&Cs immediately. Sales to present a final proposal to NetZero with the 15%/EUR 150k structure. If NetZero insists on 20% and monthly auditors we will escalate to the CEO for final signoff — please let me know ASAP.

Regards,
Laura
Chief Revenue Officer, Redwood Inference

From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.com>
To: Marta Alvarez <marta@netzerohealth.com>, procurement@netzerohealth.com
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 3 Jul 2026 18:05:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Private on‑prem + audit scope for NZ‑2384 — executive decision

Marta — thank you for the detailed requirements and for the SOW draft. Per our internal review and executive approval, Redwood can meet the majority of your constraints with the following commitments and commercial terms: 

1) Data residency: Redwood will contractually restrict production data and backups to EU region facilities.
2) Egress: Redwood will implement an approved endpoints whitelist; emergency/critical security outbound is retained under change control.
3) Auditor access: we will provide quarterly audit windows (remote sessions) and one onsite audit per year; additional sessions can be purchased. Any produced audit materials with PII will be subject to redaction rights.
4) HSM integration: we will perform HSM/KMS integration as a scoped implementation project; it will be executed under a separate SOW and requires a one‑time fee.

Commercial terms: 36‑month committed term with a 15% discount off list pricing and a EUR 150,000 one‑time implementation fee to cover custom integration and compliance work.

Next steps: (a) Legal will send redlined SOW/T&C reflecting these points today, (b) Sales Ops will update the commercial term in HubSpot (deal NZ‑2384), and (c) we suggest a follow‑up technical call next week with NetZero security to walk the SOW and integration plan.

Would Thursday 8 July for a 60‑minute technical sync work for your team?

Best regards,
David Kim
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
